title: Prove P104 rank-eight cut under arbitrary frame-path interleaving
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

The P104 channel still cannot complete its identity transfer by changing timing and scalar operations alone. This package proves a sharp rank-eight-array limit under **arbitrary interleaving of the existing per-register frame paths**, after discarding all 2,624 original ADDs, eight COPY instructions and their scalar-access dependencies. Identity on 104 ports requires rank 104 arrays.

This extends the frozen-chronology cut in #2082 (`60f4e337ffba470e09727dd435b1f1be3b67d03d`) and #2090 (`dff116efc2c4ddd7236020ad8316db5c98aa693e`) to a larger scheduling and scalar-resynthesis class. Every possible cross-register equal-frame contact is granted in a union graph, including contacts that cannot coexist in one schedule. Removing the eight original private descents still disconnects every source from every target. Each descent carries one array; its native child rank seven is not seven array wires.

Only `research/p104-commutation-cut/` is added. A useful next construction must change a frame path, storage lifetime or allowed cross-chart interface. New paths, transport replacement/fusion and additional storage remain outside the theorem. **No new kappa, native correction-price lower bound or supplier admission is claimed.**

## Validation

- Two separately implemented exact graph checkers agree on 1,698 intervals, 444 subspaces and 71,224 potential directed common-frame contacts. One uses ancestor bitsets/XOR spans; the other uses per-role traces, descendant sets and reduced binary bases.
- All 280 rational input columns recover the original `G/2` channel and restore dirty state. Exact Gram identities establish rank-eight attainment.
- Each of eight restored descent edges reopens 52 targets; the intact graph reaches all 104. A forbidden cross-frame bypass, missing dirty compensation/cleanup and frame-basis presentation controls behave as expected.
- A legal retiming moves 3,989 event positions and preserves both complete endpoints and graph invariants. Registered Python 3.12.3 optimized replay, metadata/source pins, selected-record check and whitespace check pass.
- A normal-mode source export without Git replays read-only; corrupted source and receipt controls reject. Native recompilation, global hosting, precision and all-size/outer admission are not rerun.

Reproduce:

```sh
python3 -I -O -B research/p104-commutation-cut/verify.py
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/p104-commutation-cut
```

## Credit

Credit Rohan Arun/#1972 for the channel, Chafik Boukhalfa/#1991 for native realization, Adam Gall/#1940 for its schedule, David Arias/#2082 and Adam Gall/#2090 for the immediate cut predecessors, and their geometry/decoder lineage retained in the README. Prepared by Jeremy Diviney with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in mathematics, implementation, verification and prose. Both implementations were AI-assisted; no independent human review or proof-assistant verification is claimed.

## Task and overlap

Scientific base and refreshed canonical main: `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2`, priority revision 4. Publication overlap covered 376 open PRs and 762 Discussion records with full pagination at the timestamps in `TASK.json`; relevant predecessor heads were rechecked. This is a scoped continuation of an explicitly assigned contribution effort, not a fresh lottery task. Frozen predecessors and the selected result are unchanged.

Task `p104-side-correction`, **changed scope**: attempted constructive retiming became a proof that even arbitrary scalar resynthesis cannot bypass the fixed frame paths. This does not meet the card’s construction gate. [Task and source metadata](https://github.com/jeremydiviney/integer-mult-bounds/blob/fa1a45f91c14bb4b372d19dd7d66e11fea480ef5/research/p104-commutation-cut/TASK.json).

## Open next questions

[The README handoff](https://github.com/jeremydiviney/integer-mult-bounds/blob/fa1a45f91c14bb4b372d19dd7d66e11fea480ef5/research/p104-commutation-cut/README.md#open-next-questions) proposes changing one helper’s intermediate frame, then requiring a cut bypass, arbitrary dirty-state restoration and a favorable complete native bill. No such changed word is constructed here.
